newsitem.title: USA: Funds do well in currencies, gold, coffee in Jan..
newsitem.headline: Funds do well in currencies, gold, coffee in Jan..

text.p: Commodity trading advisors (CTAs) and programs which trade the currency markets were the top peformers in January 1997 among funds surveyed by commodity and hedge fund monitor TASS Management Ltd.
All of the top ten programs for the month realised most of their profits from trades in the currency markets, TASS chief executive Nicola Meaden said.
The U.S. dollar's ongoing rally has seen the dollar make new 34-month highs against deutschmark and new 48-month highs against yen in recent weeks.
"Many funds had a good January, deriving much of their profits from trades in the foreign exchange markets," TASS chief executive Nicola Meaden said.
"Other strategies which offered good profits were shorting gold and platinum and going long such commodities as coffee," Meaden said.

Spot gold prices fell to new three-year lows this week, after a year long downtrend, while CSCE coffee prices surged to 20-month highs, after a sharp six-week rally which has seen coffee prices rise more than 50 percent.
January's good CTA returns come on the heels of strong performances by many CTAs for the 1996 year as a whole.
In the fourth quarter 1996, managed futures funds managed by TASS were up on average by 15.57 pct.
The TASS monthly report follows the peformance of 70 commodity trading programs, each with a minimum of $45 million under management.
TASS Management Ltd is a London-based research company which tracks about 1,600 alternative investment managers and funds globally who manage about $9 billion in assets.
"Alternative" investments programs include hedge funds, CTAs, managed currency programs, emerging market funds and funds of funds.
